close_reason: Fixed in ece17b3. Path A from the bead body — typed enum RequiredPermissions { Known(&'static [&'static str]), UnknownOp } replaces the &'static [&'static str] return type and the private __unknown_space_patch_op__ sentinel string. Consumers now match on the typed variant; the in-crate consumer in memory.rs validate_space_patch_ops matches exhaustively (no wildcard arm) so a future RequiredPermissions variant forces a deliberate compile-time decision rather than silently going through a catch-all. Public API change: required_permissions_for_op return type changes and the new RequiredPermissions type is added to the chat-server pub use list. Permissions module's 15 unit tests updated to assert against the typed return; 2 new tests pin enum distinctness and function pointer signature stability. Pre-1.0 / pre-publish so the API break is free. The kit's existing typed-enum-over-string preference (EmojiSetOp, ChatLimits) was endorsed by the bead body — this fix follows that precedent.
description:
File: crate-jmap-chat-server/src/permissions.rs:50-122

  const UNKNOWN_OP_SENTINEL: &str = "__unknown_space_patch_op__";

  pub fn required_permissions_for_op(op: &SpacePatchOp) -> &'static [&'static str] {
      match op {
          // ...
          _ => &[UNKNOWN_OP_SENTINEL],
      }
  }

The fail-closed posture for unknown SpacePatchOp variants is
correct — SpacePatchOp is #[non_exhaustive] upstream so a
downstream caller can't compile-time enumerate. JMAP-x2gd.25 (P3)
already endorses the fail-closed intent.

But the SIGNAL MECHANISM forces every consuming backend to write
defensive boilerplate:

  let required = required_permissions_for_op(op);
  if required.contains(&"__unknown_space_patch_op__") {
      return reject_with_forbidden();
  }
  // ...check permissions normally

Three problems:

1. The sentinel string is PRIVATE (`const UNKNOWN_OP_SENTINEL`)
   but the contract REQUIRES consumers to check for it. A naive
   consumer who doesn't read the rustdoc closely just sees:
   'permissions list contains some weird string; treat as
   permission requirement; call user.has_permission("__unknown_space_patch_op__");
   which returns false; reject.' That is the intended behavior
   by accident. The contract is load-bearing on a name no public
   API exposes.

2. If the sentinel ever changes — e.g. a future revision wants
   the variant tag inside the sentinel for diagnostics, like
   "__unknown_space_patch_op:SomeNewVariant__" — every backend
   that literally pattern-matched the original string is
   silently broken.

3. The return type Vec<&str> overloads two roles: 'list of
   permissions the caller must hold' and 'this variant is
   unrecognized, give up'. Two contracts in one channel.

Fix options:

A. Change the return type to give the unknown case its own arm:

     pub enum RequiredPermissions {
         Known(&'static [&'static str]),
         UnknownOp,
     }
     pub fn required_permissions_for_op(op: &SpacePatchOp) -> RequiredPermissions

   Consumers match on the enum. Compile-time guarantee that the
   two cases are distinguished. #[non_exhaustive] on the enum to
   preserve forward-compat for a future Known+Conditional shape.

B. (Lighter) Make the sentinel `pub` with a stable name:

     pub const UNKNOWN_OP_SENTINEL: &str = "__unknown_space_patch_op__";

   Then document that backends MUST check for == UNKNOWN_OP_SENTINEL
   or use a contains-by-reference comparison. Less type-safe than
   A but unblocks consumers from the magic-string lottery.

Option A is the workspace-shaped fix; the kit already prefers
typed enums over sentinel strings (cf. EmojiSetOp, ChatLimits).

(Note: this is a different concern from JMAP-x2gd.25 which simply
records that the fail-closed posture is correct. This finding is
about the contract shape, not the choice to fail closed.)
title: API contract: required_permissions_for_op signals 'unknown variant' via magic sentinel string
